tip: The ; ending Τι ώρα είναι; (Ti ora ine) is the Greek question mark – Greek asks with a semicolon, not ?. Its own pause mark is a raised dot (·) instead.
Τι κάνεις; (Ti kanis) on its own is the greeting 'how are you?'. Adding a topic like το πρωί (to proi = in the morning) turns it back into a real 'what do you do?'.
Prices 'make' in Greek: κάνει (kani) in Ο καφές κάνει τρία ευρώ is literally 'the coffee makes three euros'. That's normal shop talk – κοστίζει (kostizi = costs) sounds more formal.
στις δύο (stis dyo = at two) uses a plural 'the' because clock times count feminine ώρες (ores = hours). Only one o'clock goes singular: στη μία (sti mia).
No word for 'on' with days: Το Σάββατο (To Savvato) is just 'the Saturday'. Every day works this way – only the article matches the day's gender: Την Τρίτη (Tin Triti = on Tuesday).
'Which' has gender: ποια (poia) is feminine to match αδερφή (aderfi = sister). Asking about a brother, you'd switch to ποιος (poios).
Even numbers carry gender: it's τρεις (treis) because the unspoken ώρες (ores = hours) is feminine. Counting euros, 'three' becomes τρία (tria).
